sentences.text: This creature possessed a skull that was proportionally large, long, and pointed.
Small, overlapping bony scutes covered many of its vertebrae.
Two rows of these protective plates ran along the neck, back, and tail.
Additional small osteoderms also shielded the bones of the limbs.
The shoulder blade was longer and narrower than that of the related species Qianosuchus.
The holotype specimen measured 97 centimeters in total length.
The type species Diandongosuchus fuyuanensis was named in 2012.
Fossil evidence suggests Diandongosuchus ate small vertebrates like fish.
Bones of small vertebrates found near the hips likely came from the stomach contents.
Skull characteristics shared with phytosaurs, such as jaw joint shapes, likely strengthened the skull and bite for hunting.
Researchers suggest Diandongosuchus may have had a lifestyle similar to modern saltwater crocodiles.
It may have lived along coastlines without being fully marine.
However, Diandongosuchus does not show clear adaptations for a marine lifestyle.
Diandongosuchus is classified under the unranked order Phytosauria.
The genus is classified within the parent group Phytosauria.
The animal belongs to the class Reptilia.
The type species of the genus is Diandongosuchus fuyuanensis.
It is closely related to Qianosuchus, an aquatic pseudosuchian that is the second most basal member of Poposauroidea.
Later studies by Stocker et al. (2016, 2017) reclassified Diandongosuchus as the basalmost known phytosaur.
Diandongosuchus lived during the Middle Triassic period in China.
The species lived during the Ladinian stage, between 241.464 and 237 million years ago.
Diandongosuchus fossils were found in a Ladinian-age marine limestone formation.
The fossil association likely represents environments along the northern coasts of the Tethys Sea.
